summary: 67 raw findings from 7 finders were merged into 46 findings. Merges: focal-loss bug [trainloop-01, data-01, dynamics-3]; single-run/noise [trainloop-03, data-06, dynamics-5, literature-4]; grid search on pre-gate model [trainloop-04, data-02, dynamics-7, provenance-06]; HEAD selection criterion change [trainloop-05, provenance-09]; protocol constants unpinned [trainloop-06, model-09, data-05]; gate non-identifiability [model-05, dynamics-1]; gate collapse [model-06, dynamics-2]; os.chdir/pyvis [model-08, provenance-02]; node-feature redundancy [graph-04, literature-2, data-10]; BigVul label noise [data-04, literature-3]; checkpoint selection/threshold moot [data-07, dynamics-4]; under-trained baseline vs literature [literature-5, data-08]; depth ablation flat but pre-gate [dynamics-6, provenance-08]; Figure 2 unreproducible [provenance-01, dynamics-8]. All other raw findings kept as distinct. No raw finding was excluded entirely as unsupported speculation; parts within findings that are speculative are marked as such in the claims: trainloop-08's assertion that OOM skipping affected Table 1 (no evidence it fired, kept at confidence 0.3), data-03's claim that the 1200-char filter halves the positive rate (unverifiable without data), trainloop-02/data-02/trainloop-01's suggestion that the hybrid is differentially harmed by the stream/loss defects (no measurement), and dynamics-3's 'no renormalisation' mechanism (superseded by trainloop-01's computation showing plain weighted CE gives a 1:1 gradient share; the 4.2:1 imbalance comes from alpha being exponentiated into p_t). One severity judgement: provenance-02 (hard-coded os.chdir) was reported critical; merged as major because it is a two-line path error that blocks import but changes no number. Overall picture for the user's question: confirmed code bugs that specifically cripple the graph branch (edge-type labelling, <global> duplicates, C++-as-C stubs, un-normalised features) coexist with design choices that make the graph branch redundant by construction (frozen CLS of the same text, 1200-char filter) and a measurement too coarse (one unseeded run per arm, 1.9-point gap) to say the hybrid is worse at all; the thesis's Figure 2 interpretation is not supported by the architecture or by the repo's own replicate runs.

findings.title: FocalLoss applies the class weight inside cross_entropy before computing p_t: the trained loss is -w_t(1-p_t^{w_t})^2 log p_t, removing focal damping for positives, over-damping negatives, and starting every focal-era run in an all-positive regime
findings.claim: [trainloop-01, data-01, dynamics-3] In both thesis-era and HEAD FocalLoss.forward, ce = F.cross_entropy(..., weight=alpha, reduction='none') and pt = exp(-ce), so pt = p_t^{alpha_t}, not p_t. With alpha = 0.5/freq (w1 ≈ 16.7, w0 ≈ 0.516 at ~3% positives), a positive's modulating factor (1-p^16.7)^2 stays ≥ 0.68 up to p = 0.9 (thesis eq. 12: 0.01), i.e. 4x-240x the intended loss; a negative's factor is 0.27-0.36x the intended one. Per-batch gradient share at initialisation is 4.2:1 positives:negatives, versus 1:1 under the correct focal loss or plain weighted CE. Every focal-era 200-epoch run (plots_Elevneth, plots_12, plots_codebert_first) starts with val recall 1.0 / precision ~0.035 / F1 0.07 and needs ~25-30 epochs to reach F1 0.3; weighted-CE-era runs (both sweeps, bigvul_attn1/3/5) show no such regime (recall starts 0.03-0.4, train loss starts ~0.6 vs ~0.3). plots_selfatention never left the regime. The criterion object is shared by both arms, so this lowers both rather than biasing the comparison; §4.3's description is not what was trained.

findings.mechanism: Exponentiating the class weight into p_t makes every positive a 'hard' example regardless of how well it is classified while suppressing negatives, so the cheapest descent direction at initialisation is to push all logits toward class 1; the model then spends ~25-30 of 200 epochs recovering, probabilities are biased toward the positive class (which the val-tuned threshold must undo), per-batch gradients are dominated by whichever positive is present (bs16, ~0.5 positives per batch), and with patience 5 (CLI default and sweep setting) a run would be stopped before learning. Shared criterion: symmetric between arms. The hybrid trains its softmax gate during this degenerate phase and plots_selfatention shows a permanent collapse that a gate-less baseline cannot suffer, so a differential effect on the hybrid is plausible but not measured.

findings.mechanism: Identical minibatch sequences remove SGD's batch-recomposition noise and turn 200 epochs into 200 repetitions of one gradient sequence (modulo dropout), favouring memorisation (train loss -> ~0 by epoch ~50 while val loss plateaus, F3). If the 10% default was left on, 'trained on BigVul' is really 'trained on a fixed random 10% of BigVul train' (the prefix is random, not label-biased, because CPG_generator shuffles with seed 42; class weights counted on all train files remain appropriate). Both arms share the loader, so this lowers both; a differential effect on the arm with more fresh parameters (hybrid) is plausible but unmeasured.

Combined with the undisclosed <1200-char filter (M28: every function fits in 512 tokens) and a noisy dataset (M29), the only thing the R-GCN can add is edge information over redundant node content. Published fusion systems that report gains use node features the text encoder cannot produce (DeepDFA: abstract dataflow features excluding identifiers) or fine-tune the node encoder jointly (Vul-LMGNN).

findings.title: Published same-backbone fusion gains are 0.1-3 F1 (Vul-LMGNN, DeepDFA+LineVul); a single-run -1.9 lies inside that band and cannot distinguish 'implementation defect' from 'idea has ~zero effect here'
findings.claim: [literature-1] Vul-LMGNN (the direct ancestor of this repository, F9) with CodeBERT as backbone gains +0.10 (DiverseVul), +0.63 (Devign), +1.48 (VDSIC) F1 over CodeBERT alone, and +13 only on the 1,664-positive ReVeal set; DeepDFA+LineVul, the strongest published graph+LM fusion on Big-Vul, gains +3.17 over LineVul on the random split (93.23 -> 96.40) and +0.51 cross-project. The effect size the thesis tries to detect is therefore 0-3 F1, the same order as seed noise (M03).

evidence.quote: CodeBert 23.44 vs Vul-LMGNNs(C-B) 23.54 (DiverseVul) ... 59.53 vs 60.16 (Devign) ... 38.19 vs 51.22 (ReVeal)
LineVul 93.23 (0.31) ... DeepDFA+LineVul 96.40 (0.13); cross-project: LineVul 71.37, DeepDFA+LineVul 71.88
CodeBERT 45.74 ... Proposed (Hybrid) 43.85

findings.mechanism: A -1.89 from one run is a sample from a distribution whose published mean is 0-3 and whose seed std is ~3, not a diagnosis; the expected result of a correct implementation of this design on random-split BigVul is a hybrid within about -1 to +3 F1 of its own CodeBERT baseline.

findings.title: The thesis's two motivating citations (GALLa, EFVD) do not predict a fusion gain on Big-Vul
findings.claim: [literature-6] §2.3 cites GALLa [3] and EFVD [4] as hybrids that 'combine structural and semantic features to improve vulnerability detection performance', but GALLa discards the graph encoder at inference and reports defect-detection accuracy changes of -0.9 to +2.9 points (and -5.8 in single-task fine-tuning, 'even a large drop on the C defect detection task') on CodeXGLUE/Devign; EFVD's headline is a maximum relative improvement over the weakest baseline on unnamed datasets (full text not accessible, HTTP 403). Neither provides a same-backbone CodeBERT-vs-fusion delta on Big-Vul.

EFVD achieves a maximum absolute improvement of 35.63% in accuracy and 289.32% in F1 scores over the three publicly available benchmark datasets.

findings.mechanism: The prior the thesis should have formed from its own citations is 'small or no gain', so the observed result is the expected one rather than a surprise requiring an optimisation-difficulty explanation.
